q: What does ISDN stand for?
n: ISDN is a digital telephony standard that carries voice and data over the same lines.
ref: Philippine Electronics Code, Vol. 1 - telecommunications and signal systems

q: What does PABX stand for?
n: A PABX is a private telephone switching system serving one organization or building.
ref: Philippine Electronics Code, Vol. 1 - telecommunications and signal systems

q: What does FDAS stand for?
n: FDAS covers the detectors, manual stations, alarm devices and the control panel.
ref: RA 9514 Fire Code of the Philippines, Revised IRR (2019), Div. 12 - fire detection and alarm systems

q: What does ACD stand for in building telecommunications?
n: ACD routes incoming calls to available agents or extensions, as in a call center.
ref: Philippine Electronics Code, Vol. 1 - telecommunications and signal systems

q: What does BMS stand for?
n: A BMS is a computer-based system that controls and monitors HVAC, lighting, security and other building services.
ref: Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB), 13th ed. - building automation and controls

q: Which equipment automatically transfers the load from the utility source to a standby generator when normal power fails?
n: An ATS senses the loss of normal power, starts the standby source and switches the load over.
ref: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), Part 1 - emergency and standby power systems; Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB), 13th ed.

q: Which assembly holds the busbars and circuit breakers that distribute power to branch circuits?
n: A panelboard receives the feeder and distributes power through protected branch circuits.
ref: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), Part 1 - panelboards

q: Which device automatically opens on overload or short circuit and can be reset afterwards?
n: A circuit breaker trips automatically and can be reset. A fuse melts and must be replaced.
ref: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), Part 1 - overcurrent protection

q: Which panel monitors smoke detectors, heat detectors and manual pull stations and sounds the building alarm?
o: Fire alarm control panel of the FDAS
n: The FDAS control panel is the brain of the fire detection and alarm system.
ref: RA 9514 Fire Code of the Philippines, Revised IRR (2019), Div. 12 - fire detection and alarm systems

q: What is the joining method for PVC and CPVC pipes?
n: PVC and CPVC are joined with primer and solvent cement, which chemically welds the socket joint.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - plastic piping, solvent-cemented joints

q: What is the joining method for PPR pipes?
n: PPR is heat-fused: the pipe and fitting are heated and pushed together.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - thermoplastic piping, heat-fusion joints

q: What is the joining method for concrete pipes?
n: Concrete pipe is laid with a bell-and-spigot joint packed with cement mortar or grout. Rubber-gasket joints are also used where a watertight flexible joint is needed.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - drainage piping, bell-and-spigot joints

q: What is the joining method for hubless (no-hub) soil pipes?
n: Hubless cast iron soil pipe is joined with a neoprene compression gasket inside a stainless steel shield clamp. G.I. pipe is the threaded one, so it is the common distractor.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - hubless cast iron soil pipe joints (ASTM C1277 shielded coupling)

q: What is the joining method for HDPE pipes?
n: HDPE is fused by electrofusion couplers or by butt fusion.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - polyethylene piping, fusion joints

q: What is the usual joining method for copper water pipes?
n: Copper pipes use capillary fittings joined by soldering (or brazing for higher-temperature service).
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - copper tubing, soldered and brazed joints

q: What is the usual joining method for galvanized iron (G.I.) pipes?
n: G.I. pipe is threaded and joined with screwed fittings.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - steel piping, screwed joints

q: Which fire suppression system is best suited to an art museum, where accidental water discharge must be avoided?
n: A pre-action system uses closed sprinklers on normally dry pipe. Water enters the pipe only after a detector confirms a fire, which cuts the risk of accidental discharge on valuable collections.
ref: RA 9514 Fire Code of the Philippines, Revised IRR (2019), Div. 10 - automatic sprinkler systems; NFPA 13 pre-action systems

q: Which system has open sprinklers on empty pipes, so that all heads discharge at once when a detector trips, and suits high-hazard areas such as aircraft hangars?
n: Deluge uses open heads. When the detection system opens the deluge valve, water flows from every head, which is needed for fast-spreading hazards.
ref: RA 9514 Fire Code of the Philippines, Revised IRR (2019), Div. 10 - automatic sprinkler systems; NFPA 13 deluge systems

q: In which system are the pipes normally empty, with no permanent water supply, until the fire department connects and pumps water in?
n: A dry standpipe is a manually supplied riser, usually charged through the fire department connection.
ref: RA 9514 Fire Code of the Philippines, Revised IRR (2019), Div. 10 - standpipe and hose systems; NFPA 14

q: Which standpipe is permanently filled with water so that hoses can be used immediately?
n: A wet standpipe keeps water in the riser under pressure from a permanent supply.
ref: RA 9514 Fire Code of the Philippines, Revised IRR (2019), Div. 10 - standpipe and hose systems; NFPA 14

q: Which valve is used mainly for full-flow on/off isolation of a pipeline?
n: A gate valve gives straight-through flow and is meant to be fully open or fully closed, not throttled.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - valves; Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB), 13th ed.

q: Which valve is best suited to throttling or regulating flow?
n: A globe valve gives good flow control but more pressure drop.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - valves; Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB), 13th ed.

q: Which valve allows flow in one direction only and prevents backflow?
n: A check valve opens with forward flow and closes automatically when flow reverses.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - backflow protection; Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB), 13th ed.

q: Which valve gives quick shut-off with a quarter-turn handle?
n: A ball valve has a bored ball that rotates 90° between open and closed.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - valves; Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB), 13th ed.

q: Which valve controls the water level in a storage tank by closing as the tank fills?
n: A float valve closes as the float rises with the water level.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - water storage tanks and float controls

q: Which valve is used to lower a high supply pressure to a safe downstream pressure?
n: A pressure-reducing valve holds a set downstream pressure, as in the lower floors of tall buildings.
ref: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP) - water distribution, pressure-reducing valves
